mainTopic: Why a minor's gift is valid but his sale is not, when we check for signs of adulthood, final rulings on young people selling property, and a new משנה on dividing property verbally.
overview: The amud opens with אמימר defending his ruling that a young orphan's gift is valid. He shows that receiving money is not what decides the matter. חכמים cancelled a minor's sales because a child is drawn to money and could be tempted into selling off his father's property. They let his gifts stand so that people will be willing to help orphans. Next, רב נחמן in the name of שמואל lists when we check for signs of adulthood: קידושין, גירושין, חליצה and מיאון. He adds that selling a father's property must wait until age twenty. The גמרא explains why each item is listed: divorce covers a boy who did יבום at nine, חליצה rejects רבי יוסי, מיאון rejects רבי יהודה, and twenty rejects the view of eighteen. A string of final rulings follows, including that the twentieth year itself still counts as under twenty. Finally, a new משנה begins: רבי אלעזר says that whether a person is healthy or dangerously ill, dividing property by speech still needs a normal act of acquisition.

steps.title: If getting money makes a sale valid, would an overpriced sale count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a minor's sale could be valid because he gets money in return.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, if he sold something worth five for six, would his sale also be valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's argument, which held that a sale with money is stronger than a gift. He asks: if getting money were what mattered, would a sale where the child got more than the item was worth be valid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If receiving value were the deciding factor, then a sale where the child came out ahead (worth five, sold for six) would surely count. Since the law is that a minor's sale does not count, that cannot be the real deciding factor. So a different explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a way of turning someone's own logic against them
He sold
A sale (here: a valid sale)
So too? Would it really be so?

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
if he sold something worth five for six,
would his sale also be a valid sale?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the exchange from the end of the previous amud. אמימר ruled that an orphan's gift is valid, and רב אשי objected with a קל וחומר: if his sale, where he receives money, is not valid, surely his gift is not. Here אמימר turns that logic back on רב אשי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's קל וחומר assumes that a sale, where the minor receives money, is stronger than a gift. It reasons that if the sale fails, the gift surely fails.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: if money received were enough, even a profitable sale would be valid, yet a minor's sale is not valid. So the reason must be something else.

steps.title: The real reason a minor's sale does not count
steps.stepSummary: חכמים know a child is drawn to money, so if his sales counted, buyers could tempt him into selling off all his father's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, חכמים know that a child's mind is drawn to money. If you say his sale counts, sometimes people will jingle coins in front of him, and he will go and sell all of his father's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason minors' sales are not valid: it protects the child from being tempted by cash into selling everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether the child got fair value. The issue is that children are easily tempted by money. If sales counted, someone could jingle coins at him and he would sell off his whole inheritance. So חכמים made all such sales invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages know for certain / hold it as established
A child
Coins, money
They rattle / jingle (coins)
His father's property

phrases.english: Rather, the Sages know for certain
that a child's mind is drawn toward money;
and if you say his sale is a valid sale,
sometimes people will jingle coins at him,
and he will go and sell all of his father's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reasoning rejected in step 1 with a new explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minor's sale might count because he gets money for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minor's sale does not count, because a child is easily tempted by money and could sell off his whole inheritance.

steps.title: Why a minor's gift does count
steps.stepSummary: A child only gives gifts to people who have done good for him, so חכמים made his gifts valid to encourage people to help orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a gift, if he hadn't gotten some benefit from the person, he would not have given him a gift. חכמים said: let his gift be valid, so that people will do things for orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining the other side: why a minor's gift is valid even though his sale is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a gift there is no tempting cash, and a child gives a gift only to someone who did something good for him. Making his gifts valid lets the orphan repay kindness, so people will be glad to help orphans. So the two rules are different because the risks are different.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
Benefit, something good received
Let it be
Things, matters (here: favors, help)

steps.whatToRemember: A young orphan's sale is invalid to protect him from being tempted by money, but his gift is valid so people will want to help him.

phrases.english: But regarding a gift,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: if he had not received some benefit from him,
he would not have given him a gift;
the Sages said: let his gift be a valid gift,
so that people will do things for them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the orphans. People will help them, knowing the orphan can thank them with a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 2 by explaining the contrasting rule for gifts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a minor's sale is invalid, maybe his gift should be invalid too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gift is valid, because it is given only in return for real benefit and it encourages people to help orphans.

steps.title: When we check for signs of adulthood, and the age for selling inherited land
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: we check for signs of adulthood for קידושין, גירושין, חליצה and מיאון, but selling a father's property waits until age twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: We examine for betrothal, for divorce, for חליצה and for refusal. But to sell his father's property, he must wait until he is twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רב נחמן quotes שמואל: these marriage-related acts need a check for signs of adulthood, while selling inherited property needs a much older age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the four personal acts listed, being of age with signs of adulthood is enough. Selling land inherited from a father is treated more strictly: he must be twenty. The next steps explain why each item on this list is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We examine / check (for physical signs of adulthood)
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Divorce
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Refusal: a girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers says she does not want the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Age twenty here applies only to selling land inherited from a father. It is not the general age of adulthood, which stays thirteen for a boy and twelve for a girl.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key halachic difference: being an adult for personal matters is not the same as being old enough to sell an inheritance.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
We examine for betrothal, for divorce,
phrases.notes: We check the young person for physical signs that he or she is now an adult.

phrases.english: and for chalitza, and for refusal.
But to sell from his father's property –
not until he is twenty years old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about ages and checks for adulthood, still connected to the theme of minors and property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checks for signs of adulthood are needed for קידושין, גירושין, חליצה and מיאון. Selling a father's property requires being twenty.

steps.title: Why check again for divorce?
steps.stepSummary: If we already checked him before marriage, why list divorce as a separate case needing a check?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since we already examined him for betrothal, why do I need to examine for divorce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the list in step 4. Divorce seems unnecessary, since a man who is divorcing was already checked when he married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man can only marry once he is an adult, and the check happened then. So by the time of divorce we already know he is an adult. Listing divorce looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: And since
I (we) already examined
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And since we examined him for betrothal,
why do I need to examine for divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּבְדַקְנָא לְקִדּוּשִׁין, לְגֵרוּשִׁין לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an item in the list from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing גירושין as a separate case needing a check in שמואל's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the check before קידושין already proved he is an adult, so a second check for divorce seems pointless.

steps.title: A boy who did יבום at age nine
steps.stepSummary: The check for divorce is needed for a boy who married his יבמה at nine. He acquired her as a minor, but he cannot give a גט until he grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for יבום, as we learned: a boy nine years and one day old who had relations with his יבמה acquired her. But he cannot give a גט until he grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a case where a man is married without ever having been checked: a nine-year-old who did יבום. It brings a משנה as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through יבום, a boy of nine years and one day can acquire his brother's widow, so he becomes married while still a minor and was never checked. To divorce her he must be an adult. So at the time of divorce a real check is needed, and that is why שמואל listed divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for: introduces the specific case where a rule matters
Marriage of a man to his brother's childless widow
His brother's widow who needs יבום
He acquired her (as his wife)
Bill of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: A boy can become married through יבום at nine years and one day without being checked, so the check for adulthood happens only when he wants to give a גט.

phrases.english: It is needed only for levirate marriage –
as we learned in a Mishnah:
A boy nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama has acquired her.
But he cannot give a bill of divorce until he grows up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question of step 5 by pointing to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting to a specific case (לא נצרכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Divorce never needs its own check, because every married man was checked before marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: A boy who did יבום at nine became married without a check, so a check is needed when he comes to give a גט.
steps.raayaObject: That a minor can be married through יבום but cannot divorce until he is an adult.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדה 45a: בן תשע שנים ויום אחד שבא על יבמתו קנאה, ואין נותן גט עד שיגדל.

steps.title: Why חליצה needs a check: the woman must be an adult too
steps.stepSummary: Listing חליצה rejects רבי יוסי, who thought only the man must be an adult. We compare the woman to the man, so she must also be an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he say we check for חליצה? To reject רבי יוסי, who says the פסוק only writes 'man,' so a woman can do חליצה whether she is an adult or a minor. רב נחמן teaches us that we compare the woman to the man, unlike רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through רב נחמן's list. It explains why חליצה had to be listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about חליצה says 'man,' so everyone agrees the man must be an adult. רבי יוסי held that a woman of any age can do חליצה. By listing חליצה, רב נחמן teaches that we check the woman too, because the Torah compares her to the man.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from marrying her late husband's brother
To exclude, to reject another opinion
It teaches us (something new)
We compare one thing to another and give them the same law

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees the man must be an adult. The argument with רבי יוסי is only about the woman.

phrases.english: For חליצה: this comes to exclude the view of רבי יוסי,
who says: "man" is written in the passage,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִשָּׁה – בֵּין גְּדוֹלָה וּבֵין קְטַנָּה;
phrases.english: but a woman can do it whether she is an adult or a minor;

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמַקְּשִׁינַן אִשָּׁה לְאִישׁ,
phrases.english: so he teaches us that we compare the woman to the man,
which is not like רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why divorce was listed, the גמרא explains the next item, חליצה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why an item is needed: it rejects a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יוסי, only the man would need to be checked for חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman is compared to the man, so she must also show signs of adulthood.

steps.title: Why מיאון needs a check: two hairs end the right to refuse
steps.stepSummary: Listing מיאון rejects רבי יהודה, who allowed refusal until full maturity. Once the signs of adulthood appear, she can no longer refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he say we check for מיאון? To reject רבי יהודה, who says she can refuse until the black hair covers most of the area. רב נחמן teaches us that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item on the list, מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl married off as a minor can cancel the marriage by refusing, which is called מיאון. רבי יהודה said she keeps this right until she is fully mature. רב נחמן teaches that the simple check for signs of adulthood is enough, so once they appear she can no longer refuse.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: a girl married off as a minor cancels the marriage
Until the black hair is greater, meaning full maturity

phrases.english: And for refusal: this comes to exclude the view of רבי יהודה,
who says: she can refuse until the black is greater;
phrases.notes: He means until the black hair covers more than the skin in that area, which is full maturity.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: so he teaches us that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 7, now applied to מיאון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why an item is needed: it rejects a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יהודה, a girl could still refuse even after the first signs of adulthood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the signs of adulthood appear, she can no longer do מיאון.

steps.title: Why twenty and not eighteen for selling a father's property
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'twenty' rejects the opinion that eighteen is enough to sell inherited property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to sell his father's property, he must wait until he is twenty. This rejects the one who says eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of רב נחמן's statement, the age for selling a father's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signs of adulthood are enough for marriage matters, but not for selling inherited land. רב נחמן set the age at twenty to reject a view that allowed selling at eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: His father's property, which he inherited
The one who says (an unnamed opinion)

phrases.english: And to sell from his father's property
he must wait until he is twenty:

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמַּאן דְּאָמַר בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: this comes to exclude the one who says eighteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִמְכּוֹר בְּנִכְסֵי אָבִיו עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the item-by-item explanation of רב נחמן's list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why an item is needed: it rejects a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might follow the view that eighteen is old enough to sell.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must be twenty to sell his father's property.

steps.title: During the twentieth year counts as before twenty
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: while he is still in his twentieth year, he is treated as under twenty and cannot sell yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: within the time is like before the time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final ruling that explains exactly when 'twenty' begins for selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a question of whether being in the middle of the twentieth year is enough. The ruling says no: that year still counts as before twenty, so he must finish it before he may sell.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final ruling)
Within the time is like before the time

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: within the time is like before the time.
phrases.notes: He means that during the twentieth year he is still treated as under twenty, so he cannot sell yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical detail to the age-twenty rule from step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: He cannot sell his father's property until his twentieth year is over.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the ruling sent to גידל בר מנשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends by ruling like the ruling sent to גידל בר מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows גידל בר מנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic with a second final ruling that points back to an earlier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya, רבא sent a ruling to גידל בר מנשה about when a young person may sell. Here the גמרא says that ruling is the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who received a ruling from רבא earlier in the sugya

steps.whatToRemember: Signs of adulthood are enough for קידושין, גירושין, חליצה and מיאון. Each item was listed to reject someone: חליצה rejects רבי יוסי, and מיאון rejects רבי יהודה. Selling a father's property waits until the end of the twentieth year, and the הלכה follows the ruling sent to גידל בר מנשה.

phrases.english: And the הלכה follows גידל בר מנשה.
phrases.notes: This points back to the ruling רבא sent to גידל בר מנשה earlier in the sugya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second final ruling that wraps up the discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling sent to גידל בר מנשה is the accepted הלכה.

steps.title: Final rulings like מר זוטרא, אמימר, and רב נחמן in the name of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three final rulings that close the topic. The הלכה follows מר זוטרא, אמימר, and רב נחמן quoting שמואל in all his statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like מר זוטרא. The הלכה is like אמימר. And the הלכה is like what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל, in all of those matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the whole discussion by stating, one after another, whose opinions are the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ruling points back to a statement made earlier in the sugya. מר זוטרא said that someone who cannot sell land also cannot testify about land. אמימר said that an orphan under twenty can still give gifts from what he inherited. The word בכולהו means that every one of שמואל's statements, as quoted by רב נחמן, is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
In all of them, meaning every one of the statements

steps.whatToRemember: The sugya ends with practical rulings. The הלכה follows מר זוטרא and אמימר, and follows all of the statements רב נחמן quoted from שמואל.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Mar Zutra.
And the halacha is like Ameimar.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל – בְּכוּלְּהוּ.
phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rav Nachman, who said in the name of Shmuel, in all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the run of final rulings that began in steps 10 and 11, and closes the topic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical הלכה follows מר זוטרא, אמימר, and every statement רב נחמן quoted from שמואל.

steps.title: New משנה: dividing property by verbal instruction
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי אלעזר says that whether the person is healthy or dangerously ill, land is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession, and movable items only through pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person divides his property by speaking. רבי אלעזר says that the rule is the same for a healthy person and for a dangerously ill person. Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land, is acquired with money, with a document, or by taking possession. Property that does not serve as a guarantee, meaning movable items, is acquired only by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי אלעזר teaches that dividing property just by speaking follows the normal rules of acquisition, even for someone who is dangerously ill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person who hands out his property using only words. רבי אלעזר does not make an exception for a מסוכן: both a healthy person and a sick person need a proper act of acquisition. For land that act is כסף, שטר, or חזקה, and for movable items it is only משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who divides his property by his mouth, meaning by verbal instruction only
A healthy person
A dangerously ill person
Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land
Taking possession, by doing an act of ownership on land
Pulling, the way movable items are acquired

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'by his mouth' as meaning that his words alone finish the transfer. According to רבי אלעזר, the recipients still need a real act of acquisition, even when the giver is dangerously ill.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who divides his property by his mouth,
Rabbi Elazar says:
Both a healthy person and a dangerously ill person, the same rule applies:
Property that serves as a guarantee
phrases.notes: This is land, which can back up a debt.

phrases.english: is acquired with money, with a document, or by taking possession,
and property that does not serve as a guarantee
is acquired only by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ended with its final rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a healthy person and a dangerously ill person who divide property verbally follow the same rule. Land is acquired through כסף, שטר, or חזקה, and movable items only through משיכה.
